system_note: Summary judgment for entire stay (DRG): The medical record supports most trauma-related diagnoses and the operative/procedural coding (splenectomy, pelvic external fixation, femoral IMN, chest tube, transfusion, IR pelvic embolization, prolonged ventilation), but multiple diagnosis-level errors were identified that change CC/MCC status and remove unsupported codes. Key points with citations below: 1) Principal diagnosis / Splenic injury (position 1: S36.032A, billed MCC) - SUPPORTED as principal and MCC: CT trauma panscan documents a Grade IV splenic laceration with active extravasation and trauma/operative notes document emergent splenectomy. Policy requires AAST grade or operative confirmation for S36.032A; both are present (operative attribution + radiology grade + post-splenectomy vaccinations documented). Evidence: Diagnostic Imaging Report - CT Trauma Panscan (p. 448) and Trauma Surgery Consultation (p. 47); Splenic Injury policy (Policy Documents/DRG/Splenic Injury.docx) validates Grade IV as MCC and accepts operative documentation as grade confirmation. Conclusion: leave S36.032A as principal (position 1), POA=Y, MCC. 2) Pelvic ring fracture (billed S32.810A, CC) - MISCLASSIFIED: documentation shows an "open-book"/Tile B-type unstable ring (H&P: "Pelvis: unstable to lateral compression; pelvic binder applied" and CT: symphyseal diastasis 3.5 cm with bilateral posterior SI disruption and active extravasation) and the patient underwent external fixation. Policy explicitly distinguishes stable (S32.810A, CC) from unstable (S32.811A, MCC) and requires the surgeon's stability attribution; that attribution is present in the chart. Therefore S32.810A should be recoded to S32.811A (unstable, MCC). Evidence: History & Physical (Admitting) and CT Trauma Panscan (p. 448); Pelvic Ring Disruption policy (Policy Documents/DRG/Pelvic Ring Disruption.docx). Action: change to S32.811A (MCC). 3) Traumatic shock vs cardiogenic shock (T79.4XXA billed MCC; R57.01 billed MCC) - PARTIAL ISSUE: chart documents hemorrhagic/traumatic shock (MTP activation, hypotension at presentation, operative hemorrhage control and IR embolization) consistent with T79.4XXA MCC. There is no clinical evidence of cardiogenic shock (troponin negative, no documentation of pump failure/myocardial contusion/tamponade). The billed R57.01 (cardiogenic shock) is not supported by the record and should be removed. Evidence: History & Physical (Admitting) (admission vitals, MTP and OR for hemorrhage control) and lab phrase "troponin negative"; Traumatic Shock policy (Policy Documents/DRG/Traumatic Shock.docx) lists MTP/operative hemorrhage control as supporting traumatic shock. Action: retain T79.4XXA (MCC) but remove R57.01. 4) Acute posthemorrhagic anemia (D62) - POA FLAG INCORRECT: admission labs show Hgb 6.8 on arrival (H&P labs). The condition therefore was present on admission; the claim lists POA=N. Evidence: History & Physical (Admitting) lab line "Hgb 6.8 (initial)" and Active Problem List entry "Post-hemorrhagic anemia requiring transfusion." Action: change D62 POA flag to Y. 5) Traumatic subdural hemorrhage (S06.2X9A, billed MCC) - LACKS SUPPORT: initial CT explicitly states "Head: no acute intracranial hemorrhage; mild scalp hematoma." I could not find any note documenting a subdural hemorrhage. With no supporting imaging/operative note, S06.2X9A is unsupported and should be removed unless the provider has other documentation to justify it. Evidence: Diagnostic Imaging Report - CT Trauma Panscan (p. 448). 6) AKI, rhabdomyolysis, VAP, DVT, femur fracture, splenic/liver injuries, thoracic injuries, and operative procedures - SUPPORTED: nephrology consult documents rhabdomyolysis with CK 12,400 and AKI; problem list and discharge summary document AKI requiring RRT and later recovery; VAP (MSSA) is documented and treated; right femur fracture and IM nailing, pelvic external fixation, chest tube, splenectomy, IR embolization, and transfusion are all documented. Evidence: Nephrology Consultation (p. 256), Hospital Problem List, Discharge / Transfer Summary (p. 1093-1094), Trauma Surgery Consultation, Diagnostic Imaging Report, and operative/procedure references in H&P and discharge notes. Actions: retain N17.9 (AKI, POA=N), M62.88 (rhabdo), J95.851 (VAP, POA=N), B95.62 (MSSA), I82.401 (DVT), S72.301A (femur shaft fracture MCC), S27.4XXA (traumatic pneumothorax), S36.115A (liver contusion CC), etc. 7) Procedures: splenectomy (07TP0ZZ), endotracheal intubation (0BH17EZ), chest tube/pleural device (0WH30YZ), pelvic external fixation (0SH90BZ), femur external fixation/IMN/repair (0QH60BZ, 0QQ606Z), IR occlusion/embolization of internal iliac branch (04L33DZ), transfusion (30233N1), central infusion device (02HV33Z), and prolonged ventilation >96 hours (5A1D90Z) are supported by the operative notes, H&P, and discharge summary. Action: retain all billed procedures as documented. Net correction summary (claim-level): - Remove unsupported diagnoses: R57.01 (cardiogenic shock) and S06.2X9A (traumatic subdural hemorrhage) - no imaging/operative support found. - Change pelvic ring code from S32.810A (stable, CC) to S32.811A (unstable, MCC) based on surgeon documentation and CT findings. - Correct POA for D62 (posthemorrhagic anemia) to POA=Y (present on admission) because Hgb 6.8 documented on arrival and anemia listed on active problem list. - Retain S36.032A as principal diagnosis (AAST Grade IV splenic laceration) and MCC; leave procedures as billed. Citations (selected): Diagnostic Imaging Report - CT Trauma Panscan (p. 448); History & Physical (Admitting) (p. 849); Trauma Surgery Consultation (p. 47); Nephrology Consultation (p. 256); Discharge / Transfer Summary (p. 1093-1094); Policy Documents/DRG/Splenic Injury.docx; Policy Documents/DRG/Pelvic Ring Disruption.docx; Policy Documents/DRG/Traumatic Shock.docx; Policy Documents/DRG/Acute Kidney Injury.docx. See evidence_cited array for verbatim excerpts. Reviewer action: revise the claim to remove unsupported codes and correct S32.810A -> S32.811A (MCC) and D62 POA flag. Provider query recommended only if they can produce contradictory documentation for the removed codes (cardiogenic shock or subdural hemorrhage).
rationale_letter: To: Medical Records / Coding Department Re: DRG audit of inpatient stay MR_20 (admit 08/03/2026-discharge 12/28/2026) - Determination: Finding We performed a DRG-focused clinical documentation and coding audit of the above hospitalization, reviewing the submitted diagnosis and procedure set against the medical record and the applicable condition validation policies. The record supports a high-severity polytrauma admission with operative splenectomy and multiple definitive procedures. However, the audit identified the following errors that materially affect CC/MCC assignment and coding accuracy: 1) Unsupported diagnosis codes removed: - R57.01 (Cardiogenic shock): Not supported. The clinical documentation attributes hemodynamic instability to hemorrhagic/traumatic shock with Massive Transfusion Protocol activation and operative hemorrhage control (damage-control laparotomy and IR embolization). No provider documentation attributes shock to cardiac pump failure; troponin was negative and no operative/echo/cardiology documentation supports cardiogenic shock. This code will be removed. (Record evidence: History & Physical and Trauma Surgery Consultation.) - S06.2X9A (Traumatic subdural hemorrhage): Not supported. The initial CT trauma panscan documents "Head: no acute intracranial hemorrhage," and no subsequent imaging or operative note documents a subdural hematoma. This code will be removed unless the provider produces documentation justifying it. 2) Misclassified severity corrected: - S32.810A (Multiple fractures of pelvis with stable disruption, CC) is changed to S32.811A (Multiple fractures of pelvis with unstable disruption, MCC). Rationale: imaging documents symphyseal diastasis 3.5 cm and bilateral posterior SI disruption with active extravasation and the trauma/orthopedic documentation describes an open-book/unstable pelvic ring with external fixation performed (Tile B injury). Policy requires the surgeon's stability attribution, which exists in the record, supporting the MCC-level code. 3) Incorrect POA flag corrected: - D62 (Acute posthemorrhagic anemia) POA flag must be changed to Y (present on admission). Rationale: the ED/Admission labs show Hgb 6.8 on arrival and the active problem list documents post-hemorrhagic anemia requiring transfusion; the diagnosis was present at the time of admission. 4) Codes retained as supported: - S36.032A (Major splenic laceration, MCC) - supported by CT (Grade IV) and operative splenectomy; remains principal diagnosis (position 1), POA=Y, MCC. - S72.301A (Femoral shaft fracture, MCC), procedures for external fixation and intramedullary nailing - supported by operative notes and imaging. - T79.4XXA (Traumatic shock, MCC) - supported by MTP activation, hypotension at presentation, lactate elevation, and operative hemorrhage control. - N17.9 (AKI), M62.88 (rhabdomyolysis), J95.851 (VAP), B95.62 (MSSA), I82.401 (DVT), S27.4XXA (traumatic pneumothorax), S36.115A (liver contusion), and all billed procedures (07TP0ZZ splenectomy, 0BH17EZ intubation, 0WH30YZ chest device, 04L33DZ IR embolization, 0SH90BZ pelvic ex-fix, 0QH60BZ femur ex-fix, 0QQ606Z femur IMN/repair, 30233N1 transfusion, 02HV33Z SVC infusion device, 5A1D90Z ventilation >96 hrs) - all supported by the medical record. Correction to the claim (complete revised diagnosis and procedure sets) is provided with this letter. Please review and amend your submission accordingly. If you disagree with removal of R57.01 or S06.2X9A, provide the supporting documentation (cardiology/echocardiography documentation or subsequent head imaging/operative note) within your appeal response. Sincerely, Clinical Documentation & Coding Audit Team (References to chart excerpts and policy citations are attached in the audit system note.)

evidence_cited.excerpt: Unstable pelvic ring disruption (S32.811A) carries MCC status and reflects rotational or vertical instability requiring emergent hemorrhage control and definitive stabilization. The distinction between stable (S32.810A - CC) and unstable (S32.811A - MCC) is made by the treating orthopedic or trauma surgeon based on CT findings and classification; auditors must not infer stability from radiographic report alone - explicit surgeon documentation of stability/instability is required.
Massive transfusion protocol was activated, and the patient was transferred to the operating room for damage-control laparotomy with splenectomy, followed by IR embolization for pelvic bleeding.
